question: Who won the Best Actress in Leading Role award in the 75th BAFTA Award ceremony?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joanna Scanlan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 75th British Academy Film Awards (BAFTA Awards) 2022, held on 13 March 2022 in London, Joanna Scanlan won the Best Actress in a Leading Role award for her performance in the film "After Love". (सर्वश्रेष्ठ अभिनेत्री पुरस्कार)

 

• The Best Actor in a Leading Role award went to Will Smith for "King Richard".

 

• "The Power of the Dog" won the Best Film award at the ceremony, and Jane Campion won Best Director for the same film.

 

• The BAFTA Film Awards are presented annually by the British Academy of Film and Television Arts to honour outstanding national and international contributions to film.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 75th BAFTA Film Awards ceremony was held at the Royal Albert Hall, London, and hosted by Rebel Wilson.

 

• BAFTA also separately hosts annual Television Awards and Games Awards ceremonies.

 

NOTE

 

• Jennifer Lawrence (Option 1): American actress known for films like Silver Linings Playbook and The Hunger Games series; was not the 2022 BAFTA Best Actress winner.

 

• Kate Winslet (Option 2): British actress and past BAFTA winner in other years/categories, but did not win Best Actress in a Leading Role at the 75th BAFTA Awards.

 

• Gigi Hadid (Option 4): An American model, not an actress, with no involvement in the BAFTA Film Awards.

question:
Considering the five-year plans of India, which of the following is correct matched?
I. Rolling Plan – Introduced before Sixth Five-Year Plan
II. Mahalanobis Plan – Second Five-Year Plan
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rolling Plan was introduced by the Janata Party government in 1978, and remained in place until 1980 — i.e., it was introduced before the Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85), launched after the Congress government returned to power. (चलंत योजना)

 

• The Rolling Plan proposed three simultaneous plans: an annual budget/plan for the current year, a plan for a fixed number of years revised every year, and a long-term perspective plan.

 

• The Mahalanobis Plan refers to the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61), based on the model developed by statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, which emphasised rapid industrialisation with a focus on heavy and basic industries.

 

• Since both statements are factually correct, they are correctly matched.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused mainly on agriculture.

 

• The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85) focused on poverty removal, employment generation, and technological self-reliance.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement II (Mahalanobis Plan – Second Five-Year Plan) is also correct.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement I (Rolling Plan – introduced before Sixth Five-Year Plan) is also correct.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because both statements are factually correct.

question: Which among the following teams won the SAFF (South Asian Football Federation) Championship Women 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangladesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 SAFF Women's Championship was held in Kathmandu, Nepal, from 6 to 19 September 2022.

 

• Bangladesh won the tournament for the first time, defeating hosts Nepal 3–1 in the final. (बांग्लादेश की पहली सैफ महिला चैंपियनशिप जीत)

 

• Bangladesh captain Sabina Khatun was a key player and finished as the tournament's top scorer, playing a decisive role in the final.

 

• This victory marked Bangladesh's maiden SAFF Women's Championship title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• SAFF (South Asian Football Federation) also conducts men's, U-15, U-18 and U-19 championships among South Asian nations.

 

• Nepal, the hosts, finished as runners-up in the 2022 edition.

 

NOTE

 

• Nepal (Option 1): Hosted the 2022 tournament and reached the final but lost to Bangladesh.

 

• Pakistan (Option 2): A SAFF member nation but did not win the 2022 Women's Championship.

 

• India (Option 3): A multiple-time former champion of earlier editions but did not win the 2022 edition.

question: Hawa Mahal is situated in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hawa Mahal ("Palace of Winds") is located in Jaipur, Rajasthan. (हवा महल)

 

• It was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh of the Kachhwaha Rajput dynasty, designed by architect Lal Chand Ustad.

 

• It is constructed of red and pink sandstone in the shape of the crown of Lord Krishna, with a five-storey honeycomb-like façade featuring 953 small windows (jharokhas) through which royal ladies could observe street festivities while observing purdah.

 

• It forms part of the Jaipur City Palace complex, in the heart of the Pink City, and is a prominent example of Rajput architecture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jaipur was founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II and is popularly known as the "Pink City."

 

• The Jantar Mantar observatory and Amber Fort are other major landmarks of Jaipur.

 

NOTE

 

• Jodhpur (Option 2): Known as the "Blue City"; home to the Mehrangarh Fort and Umaid Bhawan Palace.

 

• Udaipur (Option 3): Known as the "City of Lakes"; famous for the City Palace and Lake Pichola.

 

• Alwar (Option 4): Known for the Sariska Tiger Reserve and Bala Quila (Alwar Fort).

question: Who among the following is the Union Minister for Tribal Affairs as on October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arjun Munda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arjun Munda was the Union Minister of Tribal Affairs in the Government of India as of October 2022, a position he held from 2019 in the Second Modi Ministry.

 

• He is a senior BJP leader from Jharkhand and served as Chief Minister of Jharkhand on three occasions. (जनजातीय कार्य मंत्री)

 

• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, formed in 1999, is the nodal ministry responsible for the welfare and development of Scheduled Tribes (STs) in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs runs schemes such as Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) and the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana.

 

• Arjun Munda also held additional charge of the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare for a period in 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Virendra Kumar (Option 2): Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment during this period.

 

• Piyush Goyal (Option 3): Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, and Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution.

 

• Pralhad Joshi (Option 4): Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines during this period.

question: Who wrote the "Harshacharita", a biography of Harshavardhana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banabhatta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Harshacharita" (Deeds of Harsha) is a biography of King Harshavardhana written in Sanskrit by his court poet Banabhatta (Bana) in the 7th century CE. (हर्षचरित)

 

• It is considered the first biography written in Sanskrit literature, composed in the ornate "Kavya" prose style.

 

• Harshavardhana ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE, with his capital at Kannauj.

 

• The Chinese traveller Xuan Zang (Hiuen Tsang) visited Harsha's court and left his own travel account, "Si-Yu-Ki," but did not write the Harshacharita.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Banabhatta also wrote "Kadambari," a romantic prose narrative considered one of the earliest novels in Sanskrit literature.

 

• Harshavardhana himself authored three Sanskrit plays: Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, and Nagananda.

 

NOTE

 

• Harisena (Option 2): Court poet of Samudragupta; composed the Allahabad Prashasti (Prayag Prashasti) inscribed on the Ashokan pillar.

 

• Ravikirti (Option 3): Court poet of Chalukya king Pulakeshin II; composed the Aihole inscription.

 

• Xuan Zang (Option 4): Chinese Buddhist monk-traveller who visited Harsha's court and wrote "Si-Yu-Ki" (Records of the Western World), not the Harshacharita.

question: What is an output device that transform the signal from the computer's sound card into audio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Speaker.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A speaker is an output device that converts the electrical audio signal received from a computer's sound card into audible sound. (ध्वनि उत्पादन यंत्र)

 

• The sound card itself is an internal expansion card/chip that processes and generates audio signals, which are then sent to speakers or headphones for output.

 

• Output devices display or present processed data to the user in a human-usable form — common examples include monitors, printers, plotters, and speakers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A microphone, by contrast, is an input device that converts sound into an electrical signal for the sound card to process.

 

• Common output devices include monitors, printers, projectors, plotters and speakers.

 

NOTE

 

• Plotter (Option 2): An output device used to produce high-quality vector graphics/drawings such as maps and engineering designs, not audio.

 

• Graphics card (Option 3): Processes and renders visual/video data for display on a monitor; unrelated to audio output.

 

• Monitor (Option 4): An output device that displays visual output (video/images), not audio.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "term – sports" is correct?
I. Offside – Football
II. Par – Golf
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Offside is a rule in Football (Soccer) governing a player's position relative to the ball and the second-last defender at the moment the ball is played to them. (ऑफसाइड नियम)

 

• Par is a term in Golf denoting the predetermined number of strokes a proficient (scratch) golfer should require to complete a hole or a round.

 

• Both pairings — Offside–Football and Par–Golf — are correctly matched.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Golf terms include birdie (one stroke under par), eagle (two strokes under par), and bogey (one stroke over par).

 

• Other Football terms include "hat-trick," "own goal," and "extra time."

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement I (Offside–Football) is also a correctly matched pair.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, since both pairs are correctly matched.

 

• Only I (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement II (Par–Golf) is also a correctly matched pair.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies equality before the law?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 14.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees "equality before law" and "equal protection of the laws" to all persons within the territory of India. (कानून के समक्ष समानता)

 

• It forms part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14–18), one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution.

 

• "Equality before law" is a negative concept (of British origin), while "equal protection of laws" is a positive concept (borrowed from the US Constitution) — together they ensure no person is above the law and all are treated alike in similar circumstances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

 

• Article 16 provides for equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 19 (Option 1): Guarantees six fundamental freedoms, such as freedom of speech and expression, assembly, and movement.

 

• Article 23 (Option 2): Prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar).

 

• Article 36 (Option 4): Defines the term "State" for the purposes of Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy).

question: Which Union Ministry implements the “Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0” scheme?
option_1: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
option_2: Ministry of Health and Family welfare
option_3: Ministry of Women and Child Development
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Women and Child Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0" is an umbrella scheme implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, announced in the Union Budget 2021–22. (सक्षम आंगनवाड़ी और पोषण 2.0)

 

• It merges the erstwhile schemes of Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan, Scheme for Adolescent Girls, and the National Creche Scheme to improve nutritional outcomes and early childhood care.

 

• It aims to address the challenges of malnutrition among children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers through a strategic shift in nutrition content and delivery.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anganwadi centres under this scheme are also to be upgraded as "Saksham Anganwadis," with better infrastructure, clean drinking water, and audio-visual aids.

 

• The scheme is aligned with India's National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyaan), launched in 2018.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (Option 1): Handles food security and public distribution schemes, such as the Public Distribution System (PDS).

 

• Ministry of Health and Family welfare (Option 2): Implements health schemes such as Ayushman Bharat and the National Health Mission.

 

• Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Option 4): Implements schemes for farmers, such as PM-KISAN.

question: Plant cells differ from animal cells in having an additional layer around the cell membrane termed as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell wall.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plant cells possess a rigid outer layer called the cell wall, located outside the cell membrane, which is absent in animal cells. (कोशिका भित्ति)

 

• The plant cell wall is primarily composed of cellulose, along with hemicellulose, pectin and, in some cases, lignin, providing structural support, shape, and protection to the cell.

 

• The cell wall also regulates the passage of certain molecules, prevents the cell from bursting due to osmotic pressure, and allows plants to maintain rigidity without an internal skeleton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fungal cell walls are made mainly of chitin, unlike the cellulose-based walls of plants.

 

• Bacterial cell walls contain peptidoglycan (murein).

 

NOTE

 

• Cytoplasm (Option 1): The jelly-like substance within the cell membrane that holds the organelles; present in both plant and animal cells.

 

• Vacuole (Option 2): A membrane-bound organelle for storage; plant cells typically have one large central vacuole, but a vacuole is not a layer around the cell.

 

• Chloroplast (Option 4): The organelle responsible for photosynthesis, found in plant cells but not forming a layer around the cell membrane.

question: Which among the following is not an example of the 4th Generation of Computer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ICL 2900.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fourth Generation of Computers (1971–1980) is based on microprocessors (VLSI chips); commonly cited examples include Apple II, TRS-80, STAR 1000, DEC 10, PDP 11, and the Cray-1. (चतुर्थ पीढ़ी के कंप्यूटर)

 

• The ICL 2900 Series, launched by International Computers Limited (ICL) in the 1970s, is a mainframe computer series generally classified with Third Generation computers, alongside examples like the IBM-360 series, Honeywell-6000 series, and PDP-8.

 

• Therefore, among the given options, ICL 2900 is not an example of the Fourth Generation of Computers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Third Generation of Computers (1965–1971) used Integrated Circuits (ICs) instead of transistors, making computers smaller, faster and more reliable.

 

• The Fifth Generation of Computers (1980–onwards) is based on Artificial Intelligence and uses Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI) technology.

 

NOTE

 

• Apple II (Option 1): A popular microprocessor-based personal computer released in 1977, an example of the Fourth Generation.

 

• TRS-80 (Option 2): An early microcomputer released by Tandy/Radio Shack in 1977, an example of the Fourth Generation.

 

• STAR 1000 (Option 4): A microprocessor-based computer commonly cited as an example of the Fourth Generation.

question: Tapi river basin extends over the state of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tapi (Tapti) river originates near Multai in the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh and flows westward for about 724 km to drain into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat. (तापी नदी)

 

• Its basin extends mainly over the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat, with Maharashtra accounting for the largest share of the basin area.

 

• It is one of only three major rivers in peninsular India (along with the Narmada and Mahi) that flow from east to west into the Arabian Sea via a rift valley.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tapi river runs roughly parallel to, and south of, the Narmada river.

 

• Major tributaries of the Tapi include the Purna, Girna, Panzara and Waghur rivers.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 1): Drained mainly by the Mahanadi river system, not the Tapi.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Drained mainly by rivers such as the Kaveri, Vaigai and Palar; not part of the Tapi basin.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Drained mainly by the Krishna, Kaveri and Tungabhadra rivers; not part of the Tapi basin.

question: Which Union Ministry is related to Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
option_1: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a credit-linked subsidy scheme implemented by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME). (प्रधानमंत्री रोजगार सृजन कार्यक्रम)

 

• It was launched in 2008–09 by merging the erstwhile Prime Minister's Rojgar Yojana (PMRY) and Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP), to generate self-employment opportunities.

 

• It is implemented nationally by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) as the nodal agency, in association with State KVIC/KVIBs, District Industries Centres (DICs) and banks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMEGP provides subsidies for setting up new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector for individuals aged 18 years and above.

 

• The Ministry of MSME also runs other schemes like CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises).

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Option 2): Deals with trade, commerce and industrial policy, including schemes like "Make in India."

 

• Ministry of Labour and Employment (Option 3): Handles labour welfare schemes such as the Employees' Provident Fund and ESIC.

 

• Ministry of Corporate Affairs (Option 4): Regulates corporate sector entities under the Companies Act.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "Himalayas – feature" is correct?
I. Kumaon Himalayas – lying between Satluj and Kali rivers
II. Nepal Himalayas – lying between Teesta and Dihang rivers
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Himalayas are regionally divided based on the river valleys that demarcate them: Punjab (Kashmir) Himalayas lie between the Indus and Satluj rivers; Kumaon Himalayas lie between the Satluj and Kali rivers; Nepal Himalayas lie between the Kali and Teesta rivers; and Assam (Eastern) Himalayas lie between the Teesta and Dihang (Brahmaputra) rivers. (हिमालय के क्षेत्रीय विभाजन)

 

• Hence, Statement I — "Kumaon Himalayas lying between Satluj and Kali rivers" — is correct.

 

• Statement II is incorrect because the stretch "between Teesta and Dihang rivers" corresponds to the Assam Himalayas, not the Nepal Himalayas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Punjab Himalayas are also called the Kashmir and Himachal Himalayas.

 

• The high peaks Nanda Devi and Kamet lie within the Kumaon Himalayas.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement II is factually wrong (the Teesta–Dihang stretch is the Assam Himalayas, not the Nepal Himalayas).

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement II is wrong.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement I is correct.

question:
Which of the following is correct regarding the heating of the air?
I. It expands and occupies more space.
II. It becomes heavier on heating.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When air is heated, its molecules gain kinetic energy, move apart, and the air expands, occupying more space — making Statement I correct. (वायु का प्रसार)

 

• As the same mass of air occupies a larger volume upon heating, its density decreases, making heated air lighter, not heavier — so Statement II ("It becomes heavier on heating") is incorrect.

 

• This principle — hot air is lighter than cold air — explains phenomena such as convection currents, hot air balloons rising, and land/sea breezes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Convection currents in the atmosphere, driven by unequal heating of air, are responsible for the formation of winds.

 

• The same principle underlies the working of hot-air balloons, which rise because the heated air inside is less dense than the surrounding cooler air.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement I is true.

 

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement II is false (heated air becomes lighter, not heavier).

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement II is false while Statement I is true.

question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is an employment scheme that was launched in 2005 to provide social security by guaranteeing a minimum of ________ days paid work per year to all the families whose adult members opt for unskilled labour-intensive work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 100.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), enacted in 2005, guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. (मनरेगा)

 

• It aims to enhance livelihood security in rural areas and provide social security through guaranteed wage employment.

 

• The Act was renamed from NREGA to MGNREGA in 2009; its implementation is monitored by the Ministry of Rural Development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• MGNREGA is a demand-driven scheme, and an unemployment allowance must be paid if work is not provided within 15 days of application.

 

• At least one-third of the beneficiaries under MGNREGA are required to be women.

 

NOTE

 

• 150 (Option 2): Not the standard guaranteed number of days; in specific circumstances (like drought or natural calamity), states may provide additional days beyond the guaranteed 100.

 

• 120 (Option 3): Not the number of days specified under MGNREGA.

 

• 200 (Option 4): Not the number of days specified under MGNREGA.

question: India’s First open Rock Museum is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hyderabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first Open Rock Museum was inaugurated in Hyderabad, Telangana, in June 2018 by Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh. (खुला शैल संग्रहालय)

 

• It is located near the Botanical Garden, Kothaguda, and showcases around 35 different types of rocks from various parts of India, with ages ranging from about 3.3 billion years to around 55 million years.

 

• It was developed to promote awareness of India's rich geological heritage and to educate visitors about rock formations in an open-air setting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hyderabad, the capital of Telangana, sits on the Deccan Plateau, an area rich in ancient granite and rock formations.

 

• The museum forms part of broader geo-heritage conservation efforts to popularise earth sciences among the public.

 

NOTE

 

• Varanasi (Option 1): A major religious and cultural centre on the banks of the Ganga, not associated with the Open Rock Museum.

 

• Chennai (Option 2): Capital of Tamil Nadu, known for Marina Beach and its cultural heritage, not the Open Rock Museum.

 

• Mysuru (Option 3): Known for the Mysore Palace and Dasara festivities, not the Open Rock Museum.

question: How many silver medals did India win in 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won a total of 7 medals at the 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games (held in 2021 due to COVID-19) — its best-ever performance at that time — comprising 1 Gold, 2 Silver, and 4 Bronze medals.

 

• The Gold medal was won by Neeraj Chopra in the javelin throw (athletics). (टोक्यो ओलंपिक 2020)

 

• The 2 Silver medals were won by Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting, women's 49 kg) and Ravi Kumar Dahiya (wrestling, men's freestyle 57 kg).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 4 Bronze medals were won by PV Sindhu (badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (boxing), Bajrang Punia (wrestling), and the Indian men's hockey team.

 

• Neeraj Chopra's gold was independent India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in athletics.

 

NOTE

 

• 4 (Option 1): This is the number of Bronze medals India won at Tokyo 2020, not Silver.

 

• 1 (Option 3): India won only 1 Gold medal, not 1 Silver.

 

• 3 (Option 4): India did not win 3 Silver medals at Tokyo 2020.

question: Single use plastic which have low utility has been banned in India with effect from ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1st July 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) notified a ban on identified single-use plastic items having "low utility and high littering potential," effective from 1st July 2022. (एकल उपयोग प्लास्टिक प्रतिबंध)

 

• The banned items include plastic sticks for balloons, flags, candy and ice-cream, plastic plates, cups, glasses, cutlery (forks, spoons, knives, straws), plastic packaging films, and PVC banners below 100 microns.

 

• This ban was implemented under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The manufacture, import, stocking, distribution, sale and use of these identified single-use plastic items were prohibited across India from this date.

 

• Earlier, from 30 September 2021, plastic carry bags with thickness below 75 microns had already been prohibited.

 

NOTE

 

• 1st August 2022 (Option 1): Not the actual date on which the ban took effect.

 

• 31st June 2022 (Option 2): Not even a valid calendar date, as June has only 30 days.

 

• 31st August 2022 (Option 3): Not the actual date on which the ban took effect.

question: The wet temperate type of forests are found between a height of ______ metres.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1000 and 2000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wet temperate forests in India are found in hilly regions receiving heavy rainfall, typically at elevations between 1000 and 2000 metres, such as in parts of the Eastern Himalayas, and hilly regions of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala. (आर्द्र शीतोष्ण वन)

 

• These forests consist of dense, closely growing trees, mostly evergreen species, with abundant mosses, ferns and epiphytes due to high humidity.

 

• As altitude increases beyond this range, wet temperate forests give way to Himalayan moist temperate forests and, eventually, to alpine vegetation at higher elevations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common trees found in wet temperate forests include oak, chestnut, and various species of laurel.

 

• Tropical moist deciduous forests generally occur up to about 1000 metres, giving way to wet temperate forests above that elevation.

 

NOTE

 

• 2000 and 3000 (Option 1): This range is typically associated with (Himalayan) moist temperate/coniferous forests at higher elevations, not wet temperate forests.

 

• 1500 and 3000 (Option 2): Not the standard altitude range specified for wet temperate forests.

 

• 500 to 1000 (Option 4): This lower range corresponds more to tropical moist deciduous forest zones, not wet temperate forests.

question: When was the Lucknow Pact signed by All India Muslim League and Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1916.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916 between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League at their joint session held in Lucknow. (लखनऊ समझौता)

 

• It marked a significant instance of Hindu-Muslim unity in the freedom struggle and led to the reunification of the moderate and extremist factions of the Congress.

 

• Under the pact, the Congress accepted the principle of separate electorates for Muslims, and both parties jointly demanded self-government for India.

 

• Key leaders involved included Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Congress) and Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Muslim League), who played a central role in bringing about the pact.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1916 Lucknow session of the Congress was presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar.

 

• Jinnah was referred to as the "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity" for his role in the Lucknow Pact.

 

NOTE

 

• 1911 (Option 2): The year the capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi, and Bengal was reunified.

 

• 1919 (Option 3): The year of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Rowlatt Act.

 

• 1906 (Option 4): The year the All India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka.

question: Mohiniyattam dance form gets its name from Hindu God _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishnu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam, a classical dance form of Kerala, derives its name from "Mohini", the enchantress female avatar of Lord Vishnu. (मोहिनीअट्टम)

 

• It is a solo, graceful, lyrical dance form traditionally performed by women, characterised by swaying body movements and subtle expressions (abhinaya).

 

• It combines elements of Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, and is performed to Carnatic music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mohiniyattam was revived and popularised in the 20th century largely due to the efforts of poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, who founded the Kerala Kalamandalam.

 

• The traditional costume of Mohiniyattam is a white and gold-bordered saree known as "Kasavu."

 

NOTE

 

• Kartikeya (Option 1): The Hindu god of war, also known as Murugan or Skanda; unrelated to Mohiniyattam's name.

 

• Shiva (Option 2): The dance form associated with Shiva's cosmic dance is "Tandava," not Mohiniyattam.

 

• Krishna (Option 4): Krishna, like Mohini, is an avatar of Vishnu, but the dance is specifically named after the Mohini form, not Krishna.

question: In which of the soil conservation methods in the coastal and dry regions, rows of trees are planted to check the wind movement to protect soil cover?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shelter belts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shelter belts are rows of trees planted in coastal and dry (arid/semi-arid) regions to break the force of the wind and check wind erosion, thereby protecting soil cover and crops. (वृक्षों की पवनरोधी पट्टी)

 

• This method has been extensively used in states like Punjab, Haryana and parts of western Rajasthan, where hardy trees are planted in belts to reduce wind velocity and soil erosion.

 

• Shelter belts also help reduce evaporation, moderate temperature extremes, and provide habitat for wildlife.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shelter belt programmes have been successfully implemented in parts of Rajasthan and Punjab to combat desertification.

 

• Afforestation and the planting of shelter belts are key strategies used to combat desertification in dryland regions.

 

NOTE

 

• Mulching (Option 1): Involves covering the soil surface with organic or inorganic material to reduce evaporation and prevent soil erosion, but does not involve planting rows of trees.

 

• Rock dam (Option 3): A structure built across small gullies/streams using rocks to slow water flow and reduce soil erosion by water, not wind.

 

• Contour barriers (Option 4): Involves placing stones, grass and soil along the contour of a slope to reduce water runoff and soil erosion, primarily used on hill slopes.

question: _______ is the chemical process in which different types of chemical reactions are involved in controlling the living state of the cells in an organism.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Metabolism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Metabolism refers to the sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring within the cells of a living organism that are essential for maintaining life. (उपापचय)

 

• It comprises two main types of reactions: anabolism (constructive/building-up reactions, e.g., synthesis of proteins) and catabolism (destructive/breaking-down reactions, e.g., breakdown of glucose to release energy).

 

• Metabolism enables organisms to grow, reproduce, maintain their structures, and respond to their environment by converting food into energy and building blocks for cellular components.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The rate at which the body expends energy at rest is called the Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR).

 

• Metabolic reactions are catalysed by enzymes, which speed up chemical reactions without being consumed.

 

NOTE

 

• Transportation (Option 1): Refers to the movement of substances (nutrients, gases, wastes) within an organism, not the sum of chemical reactions.

 

• Respiration (Option 2): A specific catabolic metabolic process that releases energy from food, but only one part of the broader process of metabolism.

 

• Excretion (Option 3): The process of removing metabolic waste products from the body, again only one part of overall metabolism.
